title: Grill — multiple repositories in one card (#291) — round 2
summary:
Round 1 is fully answered. This round is **only** the contradictions and gaps those answers opened — 11 items, 2 of them one-way doors.

The sharpest one: you chose `support-none-live` for `isolation: none`, but also accepted a create-validation rule that **rejects** `isolation: none` with 2+ repos, and chose a workspace root as the agent's cwd. Those cannot all hold, and `support-none-live` assumed a 'first repo' that your no-primary answer rules out.

The second: 'no primary repo' is now a real data-model change, because `Task` still has one `workdir`, one `branch`, one `worktreePath` and one `prUrl` that dozens of readers use. We need an explicit rule for multi-repo rows before the plan can be written.

Everything else is a consequence or a default: card display without a primary, the repo-selection dialog, shared-branch fallback, aggregate PR failure, issue attribution, `existingBranch`, and the exact `Repositories:` block.
proven: Round 1 settled: per-task workspace root as the agent cwd, all six issue bullets, all eight harnesses, both pipeline and issue flows, full CLI/TUI parity, aggregate commit/PR, a new `Repositories:` prompt paragraph, a fixed (create-only) repo set, best-effort archive per repo, batched git status, and the spec + e2e acceptance matrix.
Round 1 also confirmed: dedupe was not rejected, but the 'first repo is primary' and 'hard cap 10' parts of that answer were. The no-primary answer is what forces the data-model question below.

sections.title: The contradiction to resolve
sections.intro: One answer has to win. This is a one-way door: it decides whether an agent can ever write to a live repo, and whether the containment that keeps `@` safe is relaxed.

questions.title: Which `isolation: none` behaviour wins?
questions.why: It decides whether multi-repo always uses worktrees, or whether the agent can edit live checkouts — a trust-boundary change to `resolveAtPath` and the task-dir containment.
questions.context:
Your round-1 answers conflict:

- `agent-architecture` = **workspace-root** (the agent's cwd is the per-task workspace).
- `isolation-none` = **support-none-live** (the option text said the agent runs directly in live repos, with the workspace as a display path).
- `create-validation` = accepts **“`isolation: none` with 2+ repos is rejected with the worktree-required message.”**
- `primary-mirrors` = **“We don't need a primary term here”**, which removes the 'first repo' that `support-none-live` assumed as cwd.

So the current answers reject and support the same combination, and the support path has no defined cwd. Pick the one that wins.

evidence.label: today `none` means running in the source repo with no worktree
the containment a live-repo workspace would have to relax
evidence.code:
const withinCwd = realAbs === realCwd || realAbs.startsWith(realCwd + path.sep);
if (!withinCwd) return null;

options.label: Require worktrees for 2+ repos (reverses round 1's `support-none-live`)
options.description: A multi-repo task always uses `isolation: "worktree"`; `none` stays a single-repo mode. The create-validation rejection stands.
options.consequence: Consistent with the workspace-root answer, the accepted validation rule and the realpath containment. `none` users cannot use multi-repo; the UI auto-switches to worktree when a second repo is added.

options.label: Support `none` with a workspace of symlinks
options.description: The workspace root contains one symlink per live repo; the agent's cwd is the workspace. The validation clause is removed and the workspace symlinks are explicitly allowed by the containment check.
options.consequence: The agent edits the user's real checkouts (that is what `none` means) and every repo path must be allowed through realpath containment. A new, intentional security exception and a no-op teardown path.

options.label: Support `none` with copies
options.description: Copy the live repos into the workspace; the agent edits the copies.
options.consequence: Changes never reach the source repo unless a copy-back feature exists. That is not a usable `none` mode; it would need a sync/merge feature this issue does not ask for.

options.label: Support `none` with no workspace root
options.description: The agent runs in one live repo and gets the others as absolute paths; the validation clause is removed.
options.consequence: Reintroduces a de facto first repo, and Cursor/fx/OpenCode cannot see the other repos or resolve `@` into them. Contradicts the no-primary answer.

recommendation.reason: It is the only option consistent with the workspace-root answer you chose, the create-validation rule you accepted, and the containment that makes `@` safe.

sections.title: What 'no primary' means in the data model and UI
sections.intro: You rejected the primary term: every repo is equally important. That is a real contract change, because the task row and many readers still assume one `workdir`/`branch`/`worktreePath`/`prUrl`.

questions.title: What do `workdir`, `branch`, `worktreePath`, `baseRef` and `prUrl` mean on a multi-repo task?
questions.why: These columns are read by the card, filters, git status, diff, teardown, Worktrees page, CLI and older builds. Leaving them as 'the first repo' silently reintroduces the primary you rejected.
questions.context: `Task` has exactly one of each (`src/shared/types.ts:1890-1926`), and `createTask` writes one `workdir` and one `branch` at insert (`src/bun/orchestrator.ts:11030, 11298`). The git-status route and diff pick one directory (`worktreePath ?? workdir`). Your answer was **“We don't need a primary term here, all multi repos are in same level in importancy”**. So choose what those columns mean for a multi-repo row.

evidence.label: one workdir, one branch, one worktreePath, one prUrl
the single-directory readers
the card prints one path and one branch
evidence.code: {abbreviateHome(task.workdir, homeDir)}

options.label: Point the legacy columns at the workspace
options.description: For multi-repo rows: `workdir` and `worktreePath` are the workspace root; `branch`, `baseRef` and `prUrl` are null. Every repo's real branch/base/PR lives in `repositories[]`. Single-repo rows are unchanged.
options.consequence: No semantic primary, and every existing reader gets a real path. Older builds see a non-git workspace and no branch/PR; an older delete may remove the workspace root and orphan the repo worktrees. Every new reader must switch to `repositories[]`.
options.preview:
multi-repo task:
  workdir      = <dataDir>/worktrees/<task-id>   (workspace)
  worktreePath = <dataDir>/worktrees/<task-id>   (workspace)
  branch       = null
  baseRef      = null
  prUrl        = null
  repositories = [frontend, backend, infra]

options.label: Keep a compatibility mirror of one repo
options.description: One repo's branch/base/worktree/PR fills the legacy columns so old builds still show a real repo; the UI never calls it primary and `repositories[]` is the source of truth.
options.consequence: Old builds keep working per repo, but an implicit 'first' remains in the data and the no-primary claim is only true in the UI. Choosing which repo fills the mirror is itself a primary decision.

options.label: Null/ignore the legacy columns for multi-repo
options.description: Leave `workdir` as the only required path (or make it nullable) and update every reader to use `repositories[]`; no compatibility mirror at all.
options.consequence: Cleanest new model, largest contract break: `workdir` is required by `Task`, route policy, CLI and many helpers. Old builds break more visibly than with the workspace mirror.

recommendation.reason: It is the only option with no semantic primary, and it gives existing readers a real path (the workspace) instead of a null they must special-case.

questions.title: How does the card show repositories when there is no primary?
questions.why: The round-1 UI answer still said 'Card shows the primary repo plus +N', which is now invalid. This decides the card and the filter/search display.
questions.context: A card currently prints one `task.workdir` and one branch (`TaskCard.tsx:334-348`). With no primary, we cannot show 'the' repo. The repo-selection note you wrote asked for a dialog to save vertical height, so the card should stay compact too.

evidence.label: the one-repo card line
evidence.code: {abbreviateHome(task.workdir, homeDir)}

options.label: A count badge with a popover
options.description: The card shows e.g. `3 repositories`; hover/click lists each repo name, branch and PR link.
options.consequence: Compact and primary-free; the full list is one click away. The card can't show a branch at a glance, so the run panel becomes the place for per-repo state.

options.label: All repo names as chips
options.description: The card shows every repo name as a small chip, wrapping as needed.
options.consequence: No click needed, but with 5–10 repos the card grows and the board gets noisy.

options.label: One repo name + `+N`
options.description: Show one repo and a count; the popover lists the rest.
options.consequence: Most compact, but visually reintroduces a primary even if the code has none; conflicts with your no-primary answer.

recommendation.reason: It keeps the board compact and does not privilege any repo; the per-repo detail already belongs in the run panel.

questions.title: Which repo's PR gets `Closes #N` when there is no primary?
questions.why: An issue task can add repos that have nothing to do with the issue; putting `Closes #N` on all their PRs would close the issue from the wrong repo.
questions.context: `issueUrl` is currently checked against the single `workdir`'s remote at create, and the PR prefill reads the task's `issueUrl`. With no primary, the task still needs to know which repo the issue belongs to. That repo is known at create time from the dialog's `context.path` — it does not need a user choice.

evidence.label: the issue dialog knows the source repo
evidence.code:
workdir: context.path,
...
issueUrl: thread.item.htmlUrl,
issueSnapshot: renderIssueThreadMarkdown(thread),

evidence.label: the current same-repo validation

options.label: Store the issue's repo with the task
options.description: Record the source repo (e.g. `issueRepoPath`, or that repo's `repositories[i].issueUrl`) at create; only that repo's PR body gets `Closes #N`.
options.consequence: GitHub linkage survives without a primary. Adds one field and a per-repo prefill rule; the other repos' PRs are plain.

options.label: Drop `Closes #N` for multi-repo issue tasks
options.description: Only single-repo issue tasks keep the closing keyword; multi-repo PRs never prefill it.
options.consequence: No wrong-repo closes, but the user must close the issue by hand and the linkage is lost for the feature's main use case.

options.label: Ask in the repo dialog
options.description: The dialog shows which repo owns the issue and lets the user change it.
options.consequence: Explicit and flexible, but it is a choice the app already knows; adds a field to the dialog and a way to get it wrong.

recommendation.reason: The source repo is already known when the issue dialog opens; recording it keeps `Closes #N` correct without a primary.

questions.title: Same branch name everywhere — what if one repo rejects it?
questions.why: A shared branch name is your choice, but each repo can have its own `Project.branchConfig`, protected prefixes, or a name already checked out.
questions.context: You chose **same-branch** with a per-repo base ref. `createTask` renders the branch from the selected project's config and validates it; with one shared name we need a rule for a repo whose config or git refuses that name.

evidence.label: the per-project branch config today

options.label: Shared name by default, per-repo fallback
options.description: Use the same name in every repo; if a repo's config/validation/git refuses it, derive that repo's own name and show it in the repo dialog.
options.consequence: Keeps the cross-repo correlation you asked for and still lets the task start. Branch names can differ in the rare fallback case, which the UI shows.

options.label: Always the shared name
options.description: Ignore each repo's `branchConfig`; if git rejects the name in a repo, fail the create.
options.consequence: One name everywhere, but a repo with a protected prefix can block the whole task; the create error names the repo.

options.label: Go back to per-repo names
options.description: Each repo derives its name from its own config, as recommended in round 1.
options.consequence: No fallback edge cases, but loses the correlation and adds one branch field per repo in the dialog.

recommendation.reason: It preserves the one-name preference without letting a single repo's naming policy block the task.

questions.title: One aggregate commit/push/PR flow — what happens when one repo fails?
questions.why: You chose the aggregate flow. The existing parser handles one proposal, and PR creation can fail per repo (no changes, no remote, auth, already exists).
questions.context: The aggregate prompt will list every repo and branch and ask for one PR proposal per repo; one `Create all PRs` action will walk them. The question is whether one failure stops the rest or is reported per repo.

evidence.label: the one-proposal prompt today
the one-PR stamp

options.label: Per-repo best effort
options.description: Commit/push and create PRs per repo independently; show a per-repo success/failure result and allow retrying only the failed repo.
options.consequence: One dirty or unpushed repo does not block the others' PRs; needs a per-repo result model and a retry action.

options.label: All-or-nothing
options.description: If any repo fails to commit/push, stop; create no further PRs.
options.consequence: Predictable, but one repo with no remote or a dirty tree blocks the whole card. A retry redoes every repo.

options.label: Ask per failure
options.description: Show a dialog with the failed repos and retry/skip per repo.
options.consequence: Most control, most UI; still a per-repo result model underneath.

recommendation.reason: The repos are independent; a single failure should not prevent the other repos' PRs from landing.

questions.title: Repo selection dialog: where it is used and what it contains
questions.why: Your note asked for a dialog instead of inline rows to save New Task height; we need to pin its scope.

recommendation.value: One shared `Repositories` dialog used by New Task and `CreateTaskFromIssueDialog` (the Git Integration issue modal). It offers multi-select of registered projects, an `Add folder…` native picker, a base-branch field per repo, and remove. The New Task panel shows a summary line (`3 repositories`) and a `Manage` button instead of per-repo rows; with exactly one repo, today's inline branch/base fields stay. The pipeline form needs no separate dialog because it is the same New Task form.
recommendation.reason: It matches your panel-height note and keeps the Git Integration path consistent; one repo keeps the familiar form.

questions.title: Dedupe and the no-cap rule
questions.why: You rejected the primary and the cap; dedupe is still a technical necessity, and an unbounded selection needs a runtime policy.

recommendation.value: Dedupe selected projects by git root: two registered projects under one repo collapse to one worktree. No hard cap and no 400 for a large selection; show a non-blocking warning above 10 repositories (`this task will create 11 worktrees and may be slow`). Worktree creation and status polling run in bounded batches regardless of N.
recommendation.reason: Two worktrees of the same repo in one task would conflict; a warning respects 'no cap' while making the cost visible.

sections.title: Last confirms
sections.intro: Two defaults that close the remaining gaps. Confirm or override each.

questions.title: Exact `Repositories:` block
questions.why: You chose a new machine-added paragraph, which is an exception to the prompt-text rule; the plan needs the exact text and where it is emitted.

recommendation.value:
In the launch prompt only:

`Repositories:`
`- <name>: <absolute worktree path> (branch <branch>)`

One bullet per repo, no product name, no other prose. The aggregate commit/push prompt is the existing user-triggered template and names the repos itself, so it does not repeat this block.
recommendation.reason: It is the shortest block that names every repo and branch; the plan will amend the prompt-text rule in CLAUDE.md and its tests.

questions.title: `existingBranch` with multiple repos
questions.why: The current API takes one pre-existing branch; with no primary there is no obvious repo for it.

recommendation.value: `existingBranch` stays single-repo only. A multi-repo create that sends it is rejected 400 with a clear message; per-repo existing-branch selection is a separate future feature.
recommendation.reason: The issue asks for new worktrees/branches; per-repo existing branches would need N branch pickers and N collision checks.

questions.title: Confirm create-only drops the issue's 'or editing a card'
questions.why: This is the one answer that consciously narrows what the ticket asked for, so it should be explicit in the record.

recommendation.value: Confirm: the repo set is fixed at creation. Changing it means a new card. This narrows issue #291's 'creating or editing a card' to creation only.
recommendation.reason: It is the safest scope, but a reviewer should see it as an owner decision rather than a missing feature.
